description: DELETE a block event that has a handler, by the clean path, over job:block-events-reactive. The refusal is in tests/jobs-negative/delete-block-event-in-use.json; here what is proven is the ORDER that makes it pass, which is not obvious because the consumers of an event live in two different logical modules: (1) the IEventHandler of the instance, in the SCREEN - the IEventHandler is deleted alone, the block instance stays up and only loses the link; (2) the ITriggerNode, in the BLOCK - it is a node in the middle of a flow, so the predecessor is relinked to the End BEFORE deleting, otherwise the incoming connector counts as a consumer; (3) only then does the IBlockEvent leave without force, with zero consumers; (4) the REST that nobody remembers: deleting the event does NOT delete the screen action that was the handler, and it is left orphaned - without this step the Verify returns 'Warning UnusedAction: 'RatingPicker1_OnRate' action is never used in RatingDemo'. In the end the module is valid and with no new message; the button of the block still calls Rate, which now only increments the Score.

ops._why: before: 2 consumers, in different screens and blocks
1. disconnect the handler WITHOUT deleting the instance: the IEventHandler is an object of its own and leaves alone
a instancia sobrevive: EventHandlers 0, Arguments 1 (o input Caption continua ligado)
2. relink the predecessor BEFORE deleting the middle node; without this the incoming connector is a consumer
4. the rest: deleting the event did NOT take the screen action that was the handler; it was left with no consumer
without this step the Verify returns Warning UnusedAction about it
the block lost the event and kept everything else
